headline: Bias, prejudice, discrimination · 04:19

items.title: 04:19 · Anthony Greenwald and Mahzarin Banaji established the
items.detail: Anthony Greenwald and Mahzarin Banaji established the formal architecture of implicit social cognition in their foundational 1995 Psychological Review article.

items.title: 04:27 · Greenwald and Banaji define implicit attitudes as
items.detail: Greenwald and Banaji define implicit attitudes as introspectively unidentified or inaccurately identified traces of past experience that mediate favorable or unfavorable feeling, thought, or action toward social objects.

items.detail: Notice the precision of that formulation.

items.title: 04:48 · Three years later in 1998 Anthony Greenwald
items.detail: Three years later, in 1998, Anthony Greenwald, Debbie McGhee, and Jordan Schwartz introduced the Implicit Association Test in the Journal of Personality and Social Psychology.

items.title: 04:58 · That 1998 measurement instrument operationalized automatic associative
items.detail: That 1998 measurement instrument operationalized automatic associative strength by recording response-latency differentials in computerized categorization tasks.
